haiku-low.q1: No session and no sid cookie. The server creates a login_challenges row, sets a short-lived mfa cookie, and sends the user to the code page.
haiku-low.q2: Only after setup transaction C succeeds, when a valid authenticator code confirms the pending secret and sets confirmed_at. Until then 2FA is off.
haiku-low.q3: The recovery code is consumed and start_session creates a session, then the user is sent to the set-up-new-authenticator page. Sign-in does not depend on the email; an enqueue failure is logged and sign-in proceeds.
haiku-low.q4: A fifth wrong entry or five minutes elapsing deletes the challenge and cookie. The user returns to the password screen with the timed-out message.
haiku-low.q5: Transaction C deletes all the user's other sessions. The current session stays, and challenges open in other browsers are untouched.
haiku-low.q6: No. last_step is guarded by a conditional UPDATE so a step is accepted once. Drift tolerance is within ±1 step, about 30 seconds either side.
haiku-low.q7: In one transaction: pending moves to active, confirmed_at is set, old recovery codes are deleted, 10 new hashed codes are inserted, last_step is set, other sessions are deleted. If it fails, nothing changes.
haiku-low.q8: The raw token is in the short-lived mfa cookie in the browser, and only its hash is in login_challenges. Success, the fifth wrong entry, expiry or the cleanup job removes it.
haiku-low.q9: In user_totp (secret_sealed, pending_secret_sealed, pending_expires_at, last_step, confirmed_at) and recovery_codes (hashes). 2FA is on when confirmed_at is not null.
haiku-low.q10: The old active secret stays untouched, so the current authenticator keeps working and sign-in is not affected. If abandoned, the pending secret expires and the old secret and codes are unchanged.
haiku-low.q11: Exactly 6 digits is an authenticator code; anything else is a recovery code. Yes, wrong recovery codes count: any wrong entry adds to the challenge failures and the per-user wrong-entry log.
haiku-low.q12: NOT STATED as a path. The document says the LockedOut state is a dead end: support reset and identity checks are undecided, so the user cannot sign in.

sonnet.q1: No session and no sid cookie. It creates a login_challenges row (expires in 5 minutes, failures=0), sets the mfa cookie and sends the user to the code page.
sonnet.q2: When the pending secret is confirmed with a valid code (transaction C): it becomes the active secret and confirmed_at is set. 2FA is on only when confirmed_at is not null. For a replacement, the new authenticator replaces the old one at that same moment; until then the old one is used.
sonnet.q3: The recovery code is consumed (used_at set), a session is created via start_session, and enqueue_email(user_id, "recovery_code_used", {remaining}) is called after the commit. The user is redirected to the set-up-new-authenticator page with a phone-may-be-lost message instead of /home. Sign-in does not depend on the email: it is queued and sent by a background worker, and if the enqueue raises the error is logged and the user is signed in anyway (the notice is lost).
sonnet.q4: The fifth wrong entry, or 5 minutes passing. The challenge row and cookie are deleted and the user returns to the password screen with the message "Your sign-in timed out or had too many wrong codes. Enter your password again." A new challenge starts with a fresh count. A missing cookie or an expired or gone challenge also sends the user to the password screen. The per-user limit alone shows "Too many attempts, try again later" and the user must wait.
sonnet.q5: Every other session of the user is deleted (the current session stays). Challenges open in other browsers are untouched, and a valid code there gives a new session as in any sign-in.
sonnet.q6: No. The step must be greater than last_step, and it is recorded with a guarded UPDATE ... WHERE last_step < step, so a replay or simultaneous submission is rejected. The code is accepted within ±1 step (30-second steps: the current step, the one before and the one after).
sonnet.q7: In one transaction (C): the pending secret moves to the active secret (only if still present and unexpired) and confirmed_at is set to now; all old recovery codes are deleted and 10 new hashed ones inserted; last_step is set to the accepted step; all other sessions of the user are deleted. The 10 plaintext codes are returned once and never stored. If the transaction fails, nothing changes, including sessions and codes.
sonnet.q8: It is a login_challenges row (token_hash, user_id, expires_at, failures), not a sessions row. The browser holds the raw token in a short-lived mfa cookie (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax, max-age 5 minutes); only its hash is stored. It is removed on success, on the fifth wrong entry, or at expiry (5 minutes); expired ones are rejected when used and deleted by a periodic cleanup job.
sonnet.q9: Active secret: user_totp.secret_sealed (sealed with seal(), AES-GCM, key in the KMS). Pending: user_totp.pending_secret_sealed and pending_expires_at. Replay guard: user_totp.last_step (bigint, 0 before first confirmation). Recovery codes: recovery_codes(user_id, code_hash, used_at), hashes only. Enrolment status is user_totp.confirmed_at. 2FA is on only when confirmed_at is not null.
sonnet.q10: The old secret stays untouched in secret_sealed and the pending secret is stored separately; sign-in never reads the pending secret, so the old authenticator and old recovery codes keep working. Wrong codes leave this unchanged. If the replacement is abandoned or expires (assumed 30 minutes), nothing changes and 2FA stays on with the old secret and codes. Typing a code after expiry shows "Setup expired, start again" and needs the password again for a new QR code.
sonnet.q11: Exactly 6 digits is treated as an authenticator code; anything else is a recovery code (recovery codes are 10 characters and never 6 digits). Yes: any wrong entry, including an unknown recovery code, adds a wrong-entry log row and increments the challenge's failures, so it counts toward both the 5-per-challenge limit and the per-user limit.
sonnet.q12: NOT STATED as a designed path. The document marks the LockedOut state as an open dead end: product has not decided on a support reset or identity checks, and until it is decided the user cannot sign in.
